Let alpha=sqrt(kappa)+1 and beta=sqrt(kappa)-1. A_O=(1/4)*(alpha I-beta O)^T*(alpha I-beta O).
For 0<=t<=beta, ||(alpha I-tO)v|| >= (alpha-t)||v|| >= 2||v||.
alpha I-tO stays invertible; its determinant is positive at t=0 and stays positive by continuity.
sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n)*det(alpha I-beta O); positivity removes the absolute value in square-root determinant algebra.
det(O)*sqrt(det A_O)=2^(-n)*det(alpha O^T-beta I)=2^(-n)*det(alpha O-beta I).
For S subset {1,...,n}, O_(S,S) is the principal submatrix; det(empty)=1 and det of the first-coordinate singleton is U.
|det O_(S,S)|<=1, so Borel h with E|h(U)| finite makes every principal-minor weighted expectation finite. Finite sums commute with integrals.
If S contains i>=2, D_i=I-2 e_i e_i^T is orthogonal, left multiplication D_i O preserves full Haar, fixes U, and negates det O_(S,S).
Haar invariance identifies E[det O_(S,S)*h(U)] with its negative; it vanishes for S containing i>=2. Only S=empty and S={1} survive.
det(alpha O-beta I)=sum_S alpha^|S|*(-beta)^(n-|S|)*det O_(S,S); after cancellation the empty/singleton terms factor to B6.
